title: Skate or Die!
build: PAL, two-sided G64 pair supplied by the contributor (side 1 SHA-256 45e07b32..., side 2 7a402586...); EA loader, no crack or trainer

records.c: Load stub, copied here by the resident loader ($FA5B-$FA64 copies 29 bytes, $0800-$081C, from its template at $F925, which it patches per load). This copy loads file $0E (the High Jump program: $34FF bytes per the loader table at $F2F9, so $0880-$3D7E) through JSR $F230 with X/Y = $0880, sets CIA 1 port A as outputs and port B as inputs, drives $7F on port A (keyboard row 7 only) and jumps to $0880. An earlier copy in the same load (snapshot sod-hj-entry.vsf) loaded file $0C to $FDB2 and jumped to $FA69 instead. $081C is the template's 29th byte ($AD); $081D-$087F are zero and unused.

Event entry, the stub's jump target. As loaded these three bytes are JMP $0886 (first-time setup); $0893-$089B overwrite them with NOPs, so any later jump here falls through to JMP $089E, the per-entry initialisation. Self-modified: written at $0895, $0898, $089B.

First-time setup, run once per load: $01=$25 (RAM at $A000-$BFFF and $E000-$FFFF, I/O at $D000), load the font file $0F to $6800 ($1239), load and unpack the ramp picture (load_ramp_picture), load the pose and sprite data files $11 and $12 (load_skater_data), then NOP out the JMP at $0880 and fall into hj_init.

Per-entry initialisation: SEI, $01=$25, wait for the frame wrap ($0A45), black border and background, $D011=$2B (bitmap mode with the display blanked), clear zero page $12-$72 ($1304), build the quarter-square table at $0400-$07FF ($1310), build the bit-reversal tables at $2E7B/$2F7B ($1340), $1AFA, set up bitmap video and colour RAM (init_bitmap_video), the header row and sprites (init_header_and_sprites), the raster interrupt (install_raster_irq), the sound driver ($22B7) and the event state ($19C3: pass count $3A=0, one of two sprite colour schemes at random, phase 0), then CLI into the main loop.

Main loop, outside the interrupt; never returns (the event leaves through JMP $FE06 at $1A93). If $6F is set (the Commodore key turned sound off, $1A24) re-run the sound initialiser $22B7 and clear $6F. If the sound-request ring's read index $71 differs from its write index $70, take the next request ($1AA5) and pass it to the sound queue ($22F5). If the tick count $72 (raised once a frame at $0B31) is nonzero, run one step of the sound driver ($232C) and decrement it.

Load file $10 to $4000 (resident loader, X/Y = load address) and keep the end address it returns in $16/$17; run-length unpack $4000..end into $7000 ($1B6A); then copy the unpacked picture out with copy_block: $1F40 bitmap bytes to $4000, $3E8 screen-matrix bytes to $6400 and $3E8 colour bytes to $6000, which init_bitmap_video copies into colour RAM on every entry.

Load file $11 to $7000 and keep the end address the loader returns in $2E61/$2E62, then load file $12 straight after it (X/Y still hold that end). The loader table at $F2F9 gives lengths $1284 and $402C, so the files fill $7000-$8283 and $8284-$C2AF. $7000 is the base of the 30-byte pose records that set_pose_pointer indexes.

Point $29/$2A at pose record A: $7000 + A*30, with the 8x8-bit multiply at $136A (quarter squares). Each record holds five 6-byte sprite parts; byte 3 of a part is its X offset and byte 4 its Y offset (place_part_sprite). Called from place_sprites ($0BB1, $0BC9, $0BFF) and from $14F7, $1524, $1548.
Add A to the 16-bit pointer $12/$13. Not called in this load: no instruction names $096D and the word $096D occurs nowhere in the 64 KB image.

Header row and sprite set-up, part 1: CIA 1 port A outputs ($7F, keyboard row 7) and port B inputs ($FF); copy the random seed byte $2E5F to $2E60; copy 40 colour bytes from $2D8F into the top row of the screen matrix at $6400; print the inline text at $09A1 ('PASS:' and 'HEIGHT:') into bitmap row 0 at $4000 through $1242, which returns to $09CA.
Inline NUL-terminated header text printed by the call at $099E through $1242: spaces, PASS:, spaces, HEIGHT:, spaces. These are text bytes, not calls to $2020 or $4150.

Header row and sprite set-up, part 2 (after the inline text): print the string the resident code points to at $FE00/$FE01 (in this snapshot $F822, 'PRACTICE') at the start of bitmap row 0; sprite page $22=$B0; sprite multicolours $D025=1 and $D026=6; colour mask $45=$FF; copy the colour byte $FE02 into entry 4 (sprite 4) of both sprite colour schemes, $2D83 and $2D8B; starting pose $4F=$2A35[0]; build the skater sprites ($14DE); copy the two 64-byte ruler shapes $2CFF and $2D3F to $6D40 and $6D80 (sprite pointers $B5 and $B6).

Install the raster interrupt: SEI, $01=$25, CIA 1 interrupts off ($DC0D=$7F, then read to acknowledge), wait for the frame wrap ($0A45), band $1E=0, clear the raster compare's bit 8, first compare line from $2A05 ($F9), IRQ vector $FFFE/$FFFF = $0AF0, enable the raster interrupt. The NMI vector at $FFFA holds $0A3A, the middle of this routine (LDA #$0A / STA $FFFF / LDA #$01 / STA $D01A / RTS); this load never writes $FFFA, and the vector already held $0A3A in the town snapshot.

Wait until the raster line's low byte ($D012) falls, which happens when a new frame starts (PAL line $137 to 0); the 255-to-256 step reads as $FF to $00, which CMP sees as an increase, so it does not end the wait.

Bitmap video set-up: black border and background, copy $3E8 colour bytes from $6000 into colour RAM $D800 (copy_block), $D018=$90 (screen matrix $2400 and bitmap $0000 within the bank), $DD00 bits 0-1 = %10 (VIC bank 1, so $6400 and $4000), $D016=$18 (multicolour, 40 columns), $D011=$3B (bitmap mode, display on, 25 rows, Y scroll 3). Returns with carry clear.

Copy Y*256+X bytes from the read pointer $12/$13 to the write pointer $14/$15, advancing both (read_ptr12_byte, write_ptr14_byte); $18/$19 count down the low and high parts. Used by load_ramp_picture and init_bitmap_video.

Unreferenced: like copy_block but takes each byte from JSR $FFCF (CHRIN in the KERNAL jump table). No instruction or pointer names $0AA2 in this load (the two $0A,$A2 byte pairs at $1B02 and $1B30 are LDX #$0A / LDY #$00 and LDX #$0A / LDY #$07), and with $01=$25 the KERNAL is banked out, so $FFCF would run RAM. Library code carried in the program, not used by High Jump.
Unreferenced: write Y*256+X zero bytes through the write pointer $14/$15 (write_ptr14_byte). Nothing in the image names $0ABA (instruction and word scan).
Return the byte at ($12) in A and advance the pointer $12/$13; leaves Y=0. Byte source for copy_block, the run-length unpacker $1B6A and the inline-text printer $1242.
Store A at ($14) and advance the pointer $14/$15; leaves Y=0. Byte sink for copy_block, fill_block_zero, copy_block_from_ffcf and the unpacker $1B6A.

Unreferenced: JSR $FFE7 (CLALL in the KERNAL table), then repeat JSR $FFE4 (GETIN) until it returns a nonzero key. Nothing in the image names $0AE7, and with the KERNAL banked out ($01=$25) those addresses hold RAM.

High Jump raster-band update: wait for line $3A, set VIC display controls, read joystick/keyboard ports, run event update and drawing calls, then repeat late-frame work until raster $DC or ten iterations.
Read and combine active-low CIA1 ports into $2F/$30, then dispatch through the event input table at $2AB9. The following loop advances counters and calls event state/drawing routines.
State $00 handler: reset temporary movement fields, sample position and fire-related input, advance $31/$32 timing counters, update the skater display pose, and possibly switch to state $0C.
State $0C handler: update skater position, sample fire, advance $31/$32 through a pose table selected by $33, and return to state $00 when input or the table limit says so.
State $02 handler: update movement and position, select a pose from the $2A17 group by coordinate $23 and facing, then choose the next state through $2A11 when $23 crosses $96.
State $06 handler: update moving position, choose pose from indexed tables, increment $31/$32 timing counters, adjust the skater coordinate and transition to state $00 or $10 at its bounds.
State $04 handler: update movement, process directional control bits and pose flags, and choose state $02, $06 or $08 according to position and pose tests.
State $08 handler: advance an animation through seven entries at the pointer $1C, updating pose $4F every second tick, then enter state $0A.
State $0A handler: advance the same animation in reverse, sample fire at its start, update pose and return to state $04 after seven entries.
State $0E handler: advance a seven-entry pose sequence every sixth tick, choose its facing table by $24 and then enter state $10.
State $10 handler: reset temporary fields, advance a ten-tick pose sequence, choose a sprite table by stored height $2B, and on completion with fire released jump to $1A49.
Compute skater display coordinates in $49/$4A and $4B from motion indices $51/$52 and position fields $46/$47, using paired lookup differences; the sign of $48 selects the horizontal reflection path.
Pull the caller return address, read following NUL-terminated inline bytes, mask each with $3F and render its inverted glyph, then return after the terminator.
Treat A as an eight-byte index into $6800, invert each source byte, copy eight bytes to the destination pointer $14/$15, then advance that pointer by eight.
Use signed position $54/$55 and facing bit in $48 to select a two-byte position from the table at $2ACB, or clamp to an endpoint; write the result to $46/$47 and report clamping in carry.
Given indices A and Y, form the absolute index difference, use it to subtract paired lookup values at $0400/$0600 from values at $048F/$068F, and return the two resulting bytes in A and Y.
Build a 64-byte output block through the $2E7B byte lookup table: zero the unused tail, transform source bytes into destination bytes, then advance the six-byte descriptor and output pointer.
Like expand_graphics_with_table_a but map each source byte through the lookup table at $2F7B.
Build a 64-byte output block by zeroing its unused tail and copying the remaining source bytes directly, then advance descriptor and output pointers.

Toggle the output graphics buffer via $22, find a descriptor in the $7000 region from the pose index, then build four or five 64-byte graphics blocks using direct copy or lookup-table transforms according to the state sign bits.

Set High Jump phase from A (observed cases $00,$02,$06,$08,$10), reset phase counters $31/$32, and initialize distinct movement, position and sound fields for each case. The game meaning of each phase still needs a live trace.
Render the High Jump HEIGHT number from $2B: upper five bits index a two-glyph feet table at $2DC7, low three bits index rounded-inch glyphs at $2DF1, with punctuation glyphs inserted between them.

Tail of the 69-word table at $1B91 (bitmap offsets of the animated background cells, read by $192E): $1C00 is the high byte of entry 55, $1C01-$1C1A are entries 56-68, the crowd cells of text rows 9 and 10.

Screen-matrix byte (multicolour bitmap colours %01 high nibble, %10 low nibble) for each animated cell and frame, two bytes per cell (frame 0, frame 1): this label covers cells 0-31. $192E writes the chosen frame's byte to $6400 + cell offset/8. Cells 0-7 are the four flags of text row 3, cells 8-68 the crowd in rows 7-10.
Screen-matrix colour bytes, frame 0 then frame 1, for animated cells 32-63 (crowd, text rows 8-9); continues anim_cell_screen_colours.
Screen-matrix colour bytes for the last animated cells 64-68 (crowd, rows 9-10), frame 0 then frame 1; ends at $1CA4.

Colour-RAM byte (colour of %11 pixels, low nibble) per animated cell and frame, two bytes per cell, cells 0-31 here. Bit 7 of each cell's first byte is the frame flag: $192E flips it at $195A and shows frame 1 when it ends up set, so the table is rewritten during play.
Colour-RAM bytes and frame flags (bit 7 of the first byte) for animated cells 32-63; continues anim_cell_colour_ram.
Colour-RAM bytes and frame flags for animated cells 64-68; ends at $1D2E.

Bitmap pixels of the animated background cells, 8 bytes per frame, frame 0 then frame 1 of each cell (entry = cell*2 + frame), copied to the bitmap at $4000 + cell offset by $1986-$198D. This label: cells 0-3 (the two left flags on row 3).
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 4-7 (flags), at $1D6F-$1DAE.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 8-11 (crowd), at $1DAF-$1DEE.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 12-15 (crowd), at $1DEF-$1E2E.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 16-19 (crowd), at $1E2F-$1E6E.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 20-23 (crowd), at $1E6F-$1EAE.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 24-27 (crowd), at $1EAF-$1EEE.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 28-31 (crowd), at $1EEF-$1F2E.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 32-35 (crowd), at $1F2F-$1F6E.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 36-39 (crowd), at $1F6F-$1FAE.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 40-43 (crowd), at $1FAF-$1FEE.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 44-47 (crowd), at $1FEF-$202E.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 48-51 (crowd), at $202F-$206E.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 52-55 (crowd), at $206F-$20AE.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 56-59 (crowd), at $20AF-$20EE.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 60-63 (crowd), at $20EF-$212E.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 64-67 (crowd), at $212F-$216E.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 68-68 (crowd), at $216F-$217E.

156 bytes after the last animated-cell bitmap, up to the sound driver's variables. No instruction found that addresses them (opcode scan, cross-references) and none was read or written in simulated play; their pattern resembles the uninitialised call-stack bytes at $2287. Purpose unknown; probably file slack.

Number of sound IDs waiting in pending_sound_ids ($2277), 0-16. queue_sound_id ($22F5) appends while it is below $10 (a 17th request is dropped); update_sid_voices ($232C) drains it to zero each tick. Cleared with the rest of $221B-$2286 by init_sound_driver.

Lowest priority among the three slots (the one a new sound must equal or beat). Recomputed at $29BC-$29D5 after each start; set to 0 when a slot finishes ($2921), so the next request always wins that free slot.
Slot offset (0, 2 or 4) of the slot holding sound_weakest_priority: where start_sound_on_weakest_slot ($2981) puts the next accepted sound. Set at $29D8 and, when a slot ends, at $2924.
The primary-script command byte being executed, saved by dispatch_sound_opcode ($2396). Handlers test its bit 7 (BIT $221E) for the operand mode and op 7 re-reads its high nibble.
Low byte of the left-hand value for sound op 6 (compare): the slot's frequency, pulse width, sustain level, loop counter or a byte read from memory; $2220 holds the high byte for 16-bit compares.
High byte of the 16-bit left-hand compare value (frequency or pulse width) for sound op 6, compared first at $26AD.
Low byte (or only byte) of the right-hand operand of sound op 6, fetched by $26C9/$26DC from the script or through an address.
High byte of the right-hand operand for 16-bit compares in sound op 6 (set by $26DC).
Per-slot shadow of the SID frequency low byte, at $2223/$2225/$2227 for slot offsets 0/2/4 (voices 3/2/1). Written with every frequency change and read back by op 4 (add) and op 6 (compare).
Per-slot shadow of the SID frequency high byte, at $2224/$2226/$2228 for slot offsets 0/2/4; paired with slot_freq_lo.
Per-slot shadow of the SID pulse-width low byte, at $2229/$222B/$222D for slot offsets 0/2/4; set by op 1 and note command $AD, added to by op 4, compared by op 6.
Per-slot shadow of the SID pulse-width high nibble, at $222A/$222C/$222E for slot offsets 0/2/4.
Low byte of slot 0's call-stack base address (init_sound_driver stores $2287); the three slots' base pointers are words at $222F, $2231, $2233, read as $222F,x at $2608 and $2928.
High byte of slot 0's call-stack base ($22), read as $2230,x with the low byte at $222F,x.
Low byte of slot 2's (SID voice 2's) call-stack base: init_sound_driver stores $97, so slot 2 nests at $2297.
High byte of slot 2's call-stack base ($22).
Low byte of slot 4's (SID voice 1's) call-stack base: init_sound_driver stores $A7, so slot 4 nests at $22A7.
High byte of slot 4's call-stack base ($22).

Four note durations per slot, $2235-$2238 (slot 0), $2239-$223C (slot 2), $223D-$2240 (slot 4), indexed by slot*2 + bits 7-6 of a note byte. The chosen value goes to the slot's wait timer ($224D,x). Loaded by op $97 and note command $5D.

Four gate lengths per slot, $2241-$2244, $2245-$2248, $2249-$224C, chosen like slot_note_durations. Non-zero: the note sets the gate bit and the gate timer ($224E,x); zero: the note changes pitch without re-gating. Loaded by op $A7 and note command $6D.

Per-slot wait timer at $224D/$224F/$2251 (slot offsets 0/2/4): while non-zero update_sid_voices decrements it instead of reading the script, so a value N holds the slot for N further ticks. Set by op 8, notes and note commands.
Per-slot gate timer at $224E/$2250/$2252: when flag bit 5 is set it counts down each tick and at zero clears the gate bit (bit 0) of the voice's control register ($235D), starting the release.
Sound ID playing in each slot, at $2253/$2255/$2257; 0 after the slot ends. stop_sound ($2303) searches it.
Per-slot flags at $2254/$2256/$2258: 0 idle; bit 6 active (set to $40 at start); bit 5 gate timer running; bit 4 inside a script call (call stack non-empty); bit 7 paused (skipped by the updater).
Per-slot sustain level counter (low nibble used) at $2259/$225B/$225D: op $24 adds to it and writes it as the high nibble of the SID sustain/release register; op $26 compares it.
Per-slot shadow of the SID control register (waveform bits and gate) at $225A/$225C/$225E; the gate timer clears bit 0 from it, notes set bit 0.
Per-slot loop counter at $225F/$2261/$2263: set by op $31, added to by op $34, compared by op $36, and decremented by the loop op $15 (jump while non-zero).

Priority of the sound in slot 0 (SID voice 3); the slots' priorities are at $2260/$2262/$2264. Set from sound_priorities ($30AF) on start, cleared at end; compared at $29BC-$29D5 to find the weakest slot.
Priority of the sound in slot 2 (SID voice 2), read directly at $29C1/$29C8 when finding the weakest slot.
Priority of the sound in slot 4 (SID voice 1), read directly at $29BE when finding the weakest slot (slot 4 is the first candidate).
Per-slot shadow of the SID attack/decay register at $2265/$2267/$2269; set by op $41 and note command $8D.
Per-slot shadow of the SID sustain/release register at $2266/$2268/$226A; op $24 rewrites its high nibble from slot_sustain_level.

Bytes used on each slot's call stack at $226B/$226D/$226F (two per nested call); a call pushes the return pointer at stack base + depth, a return pops it. Not range-checked: more than 8 nested calls would run into the next slot's stack.
Result of the slot's last op 6 compare at $226C/$226E/$2270, as the processor's C and Z bits: 0 less, 1 greater, 3 equal. Tested by the conditional jumps of op 5 against $2635/$263B.

Per-slot octave shift at $2271/$2273/$2275: the number of right shifts applied to note frequencies before the note's own octave bits are added (note_frequency, $28E3). Set by op $B7 and note command $4D.
Sixteen-byte queue of requested sound IDs: queue_sound_id ($22F5) appends while sound_pending_count is below $10; update_sid_voices starts them newest first and empties the queue each tick.

Three 16-byte call stacks for nested sound scripts, $2287 (slot 0), $2297 (slot 2), $22A7 (slot 4), addressed through slot_stack_ptr_lo/hi. Each call pushes a two-byte return address. Not cleared by init: the bytes here are whatever the file carried; 8 levels per slot.

Sound driver reset: zero the script pointers $02-$07 and all driver state $221B-$2286, silence the three SID control registers, set volume $0F with no filter ($D418), and point the slots' call stacks at $2287/$2297/$22A7. Called at $08C8, from the main loop when $6F is set ($08D3), and at $1A90.

Request sound ID A: append it to pending_sound_ids unless 16 are already waiting (then the request is silently dropped). Called from the main loop ($08E3, IDs from the game's own request ring at $1AA5) and by sound op 2. Clobbers X.

Stop sound ID A wherever it plays: search slot_sound_id for slots 4, 2, 0 and, if found, silence that slot through $2910 with interrupts disabled. No caller in High Jump (no reference found by opcode scan); part of the shared driver.

records.s: Found: Y = the slot's SID register offset; silence the slot with IRQs masked.

records.c: Set slot A (0-2, doubled to the slot offset) to flags $80 so update_sid_voices skips it. It replaces all flags rather than setting bit 7. No caller in High Jump.
Clear bit 7 of slot A's flags. After pause_sound_slot the flags are $80, so this leaves 0 (idle) and the slot does not resume. No caller in High Jump.

One sound tick (run by the main loop once per raster frame counted in $72): start every queued ID (start_sound_on_weakest_slot), then for slots 4, 2, 0 (SID voices 1, 2, 3): skip if idle or paused; run the gate timer; if the wait timer is zero, execute script commands until a $00 byte (end of tick) or the slot ends.
Read the next byte of slot X's primary script through ($02,X) and advance the pointer; the Z flag reflects the byte (a $00 byte ends the tick at $237A).

Execute primary command A: save it in sound_command_byte, push the handler for its low nibble from $23AE/$23BE (RTS trick), and enter it with A = high nibble. Bit 7 of the command is the operand-mode flag; bits 6-4 select the sub-operation.

High bytes of the 16 primary sound-op handlers minus one, indexed by the low nibble of the command: 0 end/return ($2909), 1 set register ($23CE), 2 queue sound ($2492), 3 poke/wait ($24A1), 4 add ($250C), 5 jump/loop/call ($259B), 6 compare ($2641), 7 note stream ($26FA), 8 wait ($28F1), 9 end, A call 6502 code ($2951), B-F end.
Low bytes of the 16 primary sound-op handlers minus one (paired with $23AE); RTS lands one byte higher, on the handler.

Op $x1, set a voice register, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency (2 bytes lo,hi), 1-2 pulse width (2), 3 loop counter (1), 4 attack/decay (1), 5 sustain/release (1), 6-7 control/waveform (1). Bit 7 clear: the value follows in the script; bit 7 set: a 2-byte address follows and the value is read from there. Writes the SID and the slot shadow.
Op $02: the next script byte is a sound ID to request through queue_sound_id (started at the next tick, by priority); X and Y preserved.

Op 3 with an address operand (2 bytes). Sub-op 1 ($13/$93), wait-until: compare memory at the address with a value (bit 7 set: a literal byte; clear: a byte read through a second address); if unequal, back the script up 4 bytes and end this slot's tick, so it retries next tick. Other sub-ops ($03/$83), poke: store a value there (bit 7 clear: literal; set: read through a second address).

records.s: Unequal: rewind the script by 4 (right for the literal form $93 aa aa vv; the address form is 5 bytes long, so it would resume on its second byte), drop the dispatcher's return and go to the next slot.

records.c: Op 4, add to a register, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency += 2-byte value (bit 7 set: value read through an address), 1 pulse width += 2 bytes, 2 sustain level += byte, rewrite sustain/release and set the gate bit (re-trigger), 3+ loop counter += byte. Writes the SID and the shadows; 16-bit adds wrap.

Op 5, script flow. Bit 7 clear: $05 jump to a 2-byte address; $15 decrement the loop counter, jump while non-zero, else skip the address; $25 call (push the return pointer on the slot's stack, set flag bit 4); $35 replace this slot's sound with the ID in the next byte; others end. Bit 7 set: conditional jump on the last compare, $85 equal, $95 less, $A5 not equal, $B5 greater, $C5 less or equal, $D5 greater or equal; $E5/$F5 end.
First accepted compare result for the conditional jumps $85-$D5 (index = bits 6-4): 3,0,1,1,0,1. A jump is taken when slot_compare_result equals this byte or the one at $263B.
Second accepted compare result for the conditional jumps (same index): 3,0,0,1,3,3. With $2635 this gives equal, less, not equal (1 or 0), greater, less-or-equal (0 or 3), greater-or-equal (1 or 3).

Op 6, compare and keep the result in slot_compare_result, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency vs 2-byte operand, 1 pulse width vs 2 bytes, 2 sustain level vs byte, 3 loop counter vs byte, 7 the byte at a 2-byte address vs byte; others end the script. Bit 7 set: the operand is read through an address instead.

records.s: Bytes 2C A9 01: BIT $01A9 hides LDA #$01 at $26C3, the entry for 'greater' (result 1); entered at $26C2 it gives 0, 'less'.

records.c: Fetch op 6's one-byte right operand into sound_compare_right: the next script byte, or (command bit 7 set) the byte read through a 2-byte address.
Fetch op 6's two-byte right operand into sound_compare_right/_hi: two script bytes, or (command bit 7 set) the word read through a 2-byte address.

Op 7. Bit 7 clear ($07): play the next event of the slot's note stream at ($08,X): low nibble 0-C a note (frequency table index, 0 silent), bits 5-4 extra octave shift, bits 7-6 pick duration and gate length; $xD a note command (handler $27ED by high nibble, next byte its argument); $0E call a primary-script subroutine at the next 2 bytes; else end. Bit 7 set: $87 set the stream pointer, $97 four durations, $A7 four gate lengths, $B7 octave shift.
Read the next byte of slot X's note stream through ($08,X) and advance that pointer.

Low bytes of the 11 note-stream command handlers, indexed by the high nibble of a $xD stream byte: 0 note+duration, 1 frequency+duration, 2 note+duration+gate, 3 frequency+duration+gate, 4 octave shift, 5 durations, 6 gate lengths, 7 control, 8 attack/decay, 9 sustain/release, A pulse width. $BD-$FD index past the table (no check).
High bytes of the 11 note-stream command handlers, paired with note_command_handlers_lo; read at $2757 and jumped to through $0E/$0F.
Note command $0D: the argument is a note byte (low nibble note, bits 5-4 octave); the next stream byte is a literal duration for the wait timer. Sets the frequency without touching the gate.
Note command $1D: the argument and the next byte are a literal SID frequency (low, high); the next byte is the duration. No gate change.
Note command $2D: note byte argument, then a literal duration and gate length; starts the gate timer (flag bit 5) but does not set the gate bit itself.
Note command $3D: literal frequency (argument = low, next = high), then duration and gate length; starts the gate timer without setting the gate bit.
Note command $4D: the argument becomes the slot's octave shift ($2271,x); then the next stream event is played in the same tick.
Note command $5D: the argument and the next three stream bytes replace the slot's four note durations ($2235); then the next event is played.
Note command $6D: the argument and the next three stream bytes replace the slot's four gate lengths ($2241); then the next event is played.
Note command $7D: write the argument to the voice's SID control register (waveform, gate) and its shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $8D: write the argument to the voice's attack/decay register and shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $9D: write the argument to the voice's sustain/release register and shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $AD: the argument and the next stream byte are the pulse width (low, high), written to the SID and shadows; then the next event is played.

Note number A (0-15) to frequency in $0E/$0F: read the top-octave value from note_freq_lo/hi and shift it right by (bits 5-4 of the note byte in $11) + the slot's octave shift. Used by notes and note commands $0D/$2D.

Op 8: the next byte is a wait. $08: set the slot's wait timer (the script resumes after that many further ticks, once a $00 ends this tick). $88: set the gate timer instead and flag bit 5, so the gate is released after that many ticks while the script runs on.
Op 0/9/B-F (and every invalid sub-op): if the slot is inside a call (flag bit 4), pop the return pointer from its call stack and continue there; otherwise fall into silence_sound_slot.

End slot X: clear the voice's control register (gate off, no waveform), the slot's ID, flags, stack depth and priority, and make it the weakest slot (priority 0) for the next request. Y = the voice's SID register offset. Also called from stop_sound.
Op $0A: call the 6502 routine at the 2-byte address that follows, preserving X and Y. Sound 1 (music) uses it to call $3517, game code that picks the next phrase.
JMP ($000E): the indirect call made by sound_opA_call_code; returns to $2962 when the called routine executes RTS.

Read a 2-byte address from slot X's script and return the byte there in A and the following byte in $11 (a little-endian word), with Y restored to the voice's SID register offset. The operand form used when a command's bit 7 selects it.

Start sound ID A if its priority (sound_priorities, $30AF) is at least sound_weakest_priority: replace the sound in slot sound_weakest_slot. Equal priority wins, so a new sound replaces an old one of the same rank.

Start sound ID Y with priority A on slot X: set the slot's priority and ID, its script pointer from sound_script_addresses ($307B/$3095), clear its timers and stack, set flags $40, zero the voice's seven SID registers, then find the new weakest slot (slot 4 first, then 2, then 0) for sound_weakest_priority/slot. Also used by op $35.
SID register offset of each slot, read at even X only: $29DC (slot 0) $0E = voice 3, $29DE (slot 2) $07 = voice 2, $29E0 (slot 4) $00 = voice 1. Odd bytes unused; $29E0 doubles as nothing else.

Low bytes of the note frequency table, 16 entries indexed by the note's low nibble: 0 silence ($0000), 1-12 the twelve semitones A, A#, B, C ... G# of the top octave ($70C7 ... $D4E6), 13-15 zero. In NTSC SID units entry 1 is 1760 Hz (A6); on a PAL machine it plays about 0.65 semitone flat.
